The policy prohibits sellers from disclosing, requesting, agreeing to, or facilitating off-platform payment information; agreement to such a method constitutes a violation regardless of buyer initiation. All four seller_proposed_text instances violate the policy by actively endorsing and operationalizing an off-platform payment channel. The buyer's repeated requests for alternative payment do not excuse the seller's active proposals; the policy violation occurs at the level of the seller's proposed action itself, and all four proposals unambiguously constitute such violations in their visible context. The seller's proposal confirms agreement to net-30 invoicing and states they can issue the invoice immediately upon order confirmation. No mention of ACH direct (which would require bank details), external payment apps, or bypassing the platform occurs in the seller_proposed_text. The buyer’s mention of 'ACH direct' or 'integrated platform confirmation' does not render the seller’s response unsafe — the seller only affirms platform-compliant net-30 invoicing without specifying implementation details that would violate the policy.
